results.name: Lunex Unmasked: A New Information Stealer Deployed Through BYOVD
results.description: A sophisticated four-stage attack chain delivers the Lunex information stealer to Ukrainian-speaking users through fake CAPTCHA pages. The malware employs Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) techniques using AMD's PDFWKRNL.sys to disable kernel-level security monitoring before deploying the final payload. The stealer targets seven Chromium-based browsers, extracts credentials using custom SQLite parsers, exfiltrates cryptocurrency wallets, and establishes persistent access through PowerShell-based Chrome Native Messaging Hosts that survive binary deletion. The Lunex platform operates 28 command-and-control panels across 13 countries, features Russian-language operator interfaces, and demonstrates advanced engineering including PDB-guided kernel callback zeroing, custom encryption implementations, and direct syscall invocation. The financially-motivated threat actor originates from the CIS region and operates a Malware-as-a-Service platform serving multiple independent criminal operators.

results.name: Beyond testmetest: Native Addon Camouflage and 42 Armed GitHub Repositories Reveal a Hidden npm Publisher
results.description: Security researchers identified a sophisticated supply chain attack campaign involving 42 compromised GitHub repositories across 11 legitimate owners connected to the testmetest npm operation. The campaign evolved to use compiled native addons that decrypt hidden payloads at runtime, evading detection in CI environments through extensive anti-analysis checks. Attackers deployed polymorphic wrappers ranging from 12.9 to 13.7 MB that decode to identical publisher payloads, embedding execution hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs. The operation included credential theft, repository hijacking, forged commit timelines, and automated malicious package publishing through GitHub Actions using npm trusted publishing. The infrastructure also links to shellpanel exploitation activities targeting cPanel systems. The campaign demonstrates advanced evasion techniques including environment detection for CI systems, containers, sandboxes, debuggers, and security tools before executing malicious code on developer workst...

results.name: Beyond the Inbox: How Threat Actors Abuse Microsoft Teams External Chat for Initial Access
results.description: Adversaries are exploiting Microsoft Teams' default external chat functionality to conduct social engineering attacks and deliver malicious payloads. Analysis of over 400 incidents reveals threat actors consistently impersonate IT support personnel using throwaway Microsoft 365 tenants with IT-themed display names marked as "(Internal)" to bypass external-user warnings. Attacks frequently begin with email bombing followed by Teams contact offering assistance. Adversaries leverage legitimate remote monitoring tools like Quick Assist, AnyDesk, and ScreenConnect to gain hands-on-keyboard access, progressing from initial contact to payload execution in under 15 minutes. Infrastructure patterns show a shift from default onmicrosoft domains toward paid top-level domains, particularly .top domains comprising 50 percent of observed cases. The technique exploits legitimate collaboration features rather than software vulnerabilities, requiring organizations to implement allow-list policies and user training to disru...

results.name: Gheist: Attempted Scaled Abuse of Stolen GitHub Tokens Stumbles
results.description: Since September 15, 2026, an automated campaign named Gheist has been performing mass abuse of compromised GitHub tokens. The attack commits a workflow named sync-check to every accessible repository, designed to print repository secrets into workflow logs. These secrets are then exfiltrated through GitHub's API and the logs deleted seconds later. Over 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts have been recovered, affecting personal projects and enterprise private repositories. While GitHub's approval controls have blocked exploitation in public repositories, private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments remain vulnerable. The campaign uses no command-and-control server, carries the user agent 'gheist', and has been actively evolving with multiple variants. Approximately two-thirds of implicated accounts have been removed from GitHub, likely due to response activities.

results.name: deepveindrilling.com: Magento CMS block loader hits 953 stores
results.description: A criminal group has compromised 953 online stores, predominantly Magento shops, since July 2025 by injecting malicious JavaScript loaders into CMS blocks. The latest domain, deepveindrilling.com, was registered in October 2026 and employs sophisticated bot detection using browser fingerprinting to evade security scanners. The loader stores malicious code in visitors' localStorage for persistent execution. The campaign utilizes five different domains over 15 months, previously leveraging Keitaro traffic distribution system. Attackers exploited known Magento vulnerabilities, particularly PolyShell and SessionReaper file upload flaws, to gain initial access. The final payload targets cryptocurrency users with fake Ledger wallet pages. Most compromised stores were previously infected victims that were reinfected through persistent database access and backdoors, demonstrating the attackers maintain long-term access even after initial cleanup attempts.

results.name: Suspected DPRK Campaign staging PHP2Shell Targeting against Global PHP infrastructure
results.description: A Korean-speaking threat actor, tracked as the June 2026 Minjun campaign and linked with moderate confidence to North Korea's Lazarus Group, is actively planning targeted exploitation of two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that enable unauthenticated remote code execution. The campaign prioritizes government agencies, financial institutions, manufacturing, logistics, aviation, and trading platforms across the US, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the EU. Operators are using AI-assisted reconnaissance to rank public exploit code and plan sector-specific attacks. Exploitation attempts have been observed globally since 17 October 2026, with 17 suspected source IPs identified conducting web shell deployment and session poisoning. The vulnerabilities affect all internet-facing PHP installations below version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, with Apache mod_php at highest risk.

results.name: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
results.description: On October 21, 2026, LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was compromised and distributed through PyPI and official container images. The malicious package leveraged Python startup mechanisms to execute credential-stealing payloads automatically, without requiring applications to actively import LiteLLM. Attackers utilized stolen developer GitHub credentials to redirect the release workflow to a lookalike repository. The payload targeted authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, browsers, and infrastructure. Two execution paths were identified: a credential collector launched through path extensions and a Unix-oriented loader persisted through site-specific configuration. Collected credentials were encrypted using AES-256-CBC with RSA-wrapped keys and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The compromise affected not only LiteLLM gateway deployments but also developer workstations, CI/CD agents, test systems, and containers where Python was executed in affected env...

results.name: Infostealer riding the AI Train
results.description: Aokigahara is a newly identified infostealer with traditional data theft capabilities targeting browsers, VPN clients, cryptocurrency wallets, FTP/SFTP clients, password managers, and email applications. Its distinguishing feature is dedicated targeting of AI applications and development tools, including Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI. The malware collects authentication files, session data, and configuration files from these AI services, alongside developer credentials such as Git files, SSH private keys, and AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud credentials. Stolen AI credentials could enable unauthorized access to paid services, account resale, or data extortion. The stealer employs anti-analysis techniques including language checks, virtual machine detection, and control-flow flattening, and uses AES-256 encryption with X25519 key exchange for command-and-control communications.

results.name: ShinyHunters Renewed Mass Exploitation Campaign Targeting Oracle PeopleSoft
results.description: UNC6240, also known as ShinyHunters, has resumed mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 targeting Oracle PeopleSoft systems globally across multiple sectors including education, technology, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government. The threat actor bypassed web application firewall rules by URL-encoding a single character in the request path, accessing the vulnerable Environment Management Hub endpoint on systems where operators believed WAF rules had mitigated exposure. Following initial exploitation, UNC6240 deployed multiple web shells including x.jsp and u.jsp, a trojanized backdoor called SIDEEYE delivered via Ple64.exe, Neo-reGeorg tunneling tools, and MeshAgent for persistent access. The actor conducted reconnaissance, credential theft, and prepared for data exfiltration with established patterns indicating potential extortion activities.

results.name: PureRAT and PureLogs Campaign Targeting Japanese Organizations
results.description: Between July and August 2026, a sophisticated campaign targeted organizations across East and Southeast Asia using Japanese and Korean-language phishing emails disguised as product damage complaints. Recipients were directed to fake document-sharing websites that delivered ZIP files containing malware. The archives contained executables with double extensions and DLLs implementing various loader techniques including customized Donut loaders, Python interpreters, AMSI/ETW bypasses, process hollowing, and BYOVD attacks using vulnerable Lenovo drivers. Despite varying loader implementations, the final payloads consistently delivered PureRAT or PureLogs malware families. The campaign demonstrated advanced evasion techniques by frequently changing loader structures while maintaining the same core payloads, effectively bypassing hash-based detection methods. Infrastructure analysis revealed common sending patterns through PHP Swift Mailer and shared Feedback-ID values across campaigns.
